subject: Switchover prioritization & warm-standby acceptance
messages:
From: Derek Shaw <derek.shaw@acmepay.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Rao <legal@acmepay.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Apr 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Switchover prioritization & warm-standby acceptance

Sofia —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We dug into the proposed geo-activation workflow with the ops team and have one outstanding ask before we sign: AcmePay needs a clarified commitment for switchover prioritization and an exception to the standard warm-standby activation window.

Specifically:
- We require the ability to trigger a cross-region failover with an RTO of 20 minutes for critical routes (payments-auth, tokenization) and RPO of 5 minutes for persisted KV caches.
- We understand Redwood’s standard is 30m RTO / 15m RPO for warm-standby; we need formal acceptance of our 20/5 targets in the SOW or an alternate mitigation plan (routing priority, dedicated capacity).
- During the first 90 days post-go-live we’d like an exception to the standard warm-standby chargeback — effectively covered by Redwood while we mature traffic shaping.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can accept a carve-out or propose an alternate that our security/procurement/legal teams will accept? Priya (cc) will coordinate contract language if we get a thumbs-up in principle.

Best,
Derek
Derek Shaw
Head of Platform Reliability
AcmePay Inc.

Attachment: activation-matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Apr 2028 13:05:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Switchover prioritization & warm-standby acceptance

Hi Derek —

Appreciate the clear ask. Short answer: we can make a scoped exception but need to lock down the operational controls and escalation paths first. A few quick notes and questions so we can put workable language in the SOW/addendum:

1) Critical routes: we can mark routes as "priority" and ensure traffic is routed to dedicated warm-standby capacity with pre-warmed KV caches. We need a list of exact route IDs (payments-auth, tokenization) and an expected QPS distribution to size the reserved pool.

2) RTO/RPO: 20m RTO / 5m RPO is aggressive but feasible for a time-limited carve-out if AcmePay accepts the following operational constraints:
   - Redwood will require a dedicated standby pool (reserved capacity) for priority routes during the carve-out window; provisioning and sustained cost will be billable under the Dedicated terms.
   - We will enforce an activation-runbook and require a runbook rehearsal within 30 days of go-live.

3) Cost offset for first 90 days: we can offer a partial credit (pro-rated) rather than full coverage. Legal will need to reflect this as a non-recurring credit in the SOW.

I’m looping in Karthik to confirm product limits (cache sync, KV durability) and Marissa on contract crediting. If this is acceptable in principle I’ll get a draft addendum sent to Priya.

—
Sofia Ivanova
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

Sofia —

Thanks for the quick reply. A couple clarifications from our side:

- Route IDs: payments-auth = /v1/payments/auth, tokenization = /v1/cards/tokenize. Peak combined QPS is ~520, typical 95th = 410.
- We can agree to provisioning reserved capacity if Redwood will commit in writing to the 20/5 RTO/RPO for those routes for an initial 6-month carve-out window. After 6 months we can revisit and dial down to Redwood's standard.
- On credits: we’d prefer the first 90 days covered as a professional services credit (not a billing credit) to avoid VAT/regulatory complications in our markets.

Priya, any immediate legal objections here? If not, we’ll need Redwood to provide a short-form addendum for signature.

Regards,
Derek

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>, Derek Shaw <derek.shaw@acmepay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 5 Apr 2028 09:11:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Switchover prioritization & warm-standby acceptance

Derek / Sofia —

Quick product/ops confirmation from my side: the 20m RTO / 5m RPO for the two routes is achievable under these required constraints:

- Dedicated standby pool sized to handle 600 QPS with pre-warmed KV caches and continuous cache replication. We will use our high-priority routing table to divert traffic to the reserved pool on detection of regional outage signals.
- We must perform a full runbook rehearsal (failover and failback) before go-live. The rehearsal will be scheduled for a mutually agreed weekend window; it typically takes 3-4 hours to complete and will be documented.
- For the RPO target we will use continuous async replication with 1–2 second snapshots and a small journal window; note there is a durability tradeoff during sustained network partitions which we will document explicitly in the SOW.

Cost/credit options: Marissa and finance recommend a structure where Redwood covers up to 60% of the initial provisioning cost as an onboarding credit applied as an invoice-level credit across the first three months. Full coverage is not possible due to capital allocation.

I’ve attached an activation matrix and a draft runbook excerpt to this thread for the legal team to review. If AcmePay accepts the dedicated-pool requirement and the rehearsal precondition we can move forward with a short addendum.

-Karthik

Attachment: redwood-runbook-excerpt.docx (docx stub)

Derek / Priya —

We’re aligned. Summary and next steps: 

Summary:
- Redwood will accept a 6-month carve-out for the two priority routes (/v1/payments/auth, /v1/cards/tokenize) with operational commitment to 20m RTO / 5m RPO provided AcmePay accepts: dedicated standby pool sized to 600 QPS, a mandatory runbook rehearsal pre-go-live, and documented durability tradeoffs.
- Credit: Redwood will provide a one-time onboarding credit equal to 60% of the initial reservation charge, applied across the first three invoices. Legal will reflect this as an invoice-level credit (not a recurring discount).

Next steps:
1) Marissa will issue a short-form addendum reflecting the carve-out and credit. (Marissa: please attach the addendum draft to this thread.)
2) Priya to review and flag any compliance risks (VAT/contract flow) — please advise if AcmePay prefers the credit be structured differently.
3) Karthik/ops and AcmePay to schedule the runbook rehearsal (target within 30 days of sign).

If there are no substantive legal objections by EOD Friday we will circulate the draft addendum for signature. Thanks everyone — let’s get this across the finish line.
